messages:
cs-jen: escalation from Acme — they reported a big jump in p95/p99 latency and some 504s starting ~09:00 UTC after yesterday's runtime deploy. customer says the slowness happens when using function/tool calls with structured_output. they attached a few sample request/response payloads. cc @maria-g @aj :rotating_light:

maria-g: looking. do we have tracing + router spans for those requests? any quick mitigation we can offer the customer? :eyes:

aj: pulled traces for trace_id=trc-8f3a2. noticing a consistent ~80-140ms added per-request in the "schema-validator" span when tool calls are present. streaming is blocked until validation completes. example span tree (short):
```
router.request -> tool-router.resolve -> model.dispatch -> schema-validator.sync -> model.stream
```
median schema-validator = 6ms but p99 ~ 120ms on those hosts. tool-router overall p95 regressed ~30-40ms from baseline.

linda: graph from observability (link): https://observ.redwood/graphs/abcd1234 — p95 for route /v1/generate?tool=true jumped at deploy. also noticing retries from clients causing extra billed tokens. customer annoyed about both latency and cost.

cs-jen: they want a reproducer we can run in our env. provided payload:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-tool-1","input":"find price","tool_calls":[{"name":"search","args":{"q":"widget price"}}],"structured_output":{"schema":"price_resp_v1"}}'
```
ran it a few times locally — with schema enabled p95~220ms, with schema disabled p95~160ms (so ~60ms difference).

aj: root cause hypothesis: after the runtime change, we made schema validation run synchronously on the critical path for tool outputs (previously async for streaming models). combined with GC/CPU contention on a subset of hosts -> p99 spikes. also router now validates before handing off to cache which invalidates prefix-KV cache hits.

samir: can we short-circuit validation for known-good schemas or use a fast-path? what are options for immediate mitigation?

maria-g: short-term options: 1) customer-specific workaround: enable route setting `validate_schema: false` (per-customer override) — drops validation cost but reduces structured output guarantees. 2) enable `async_schema_validation: true` so we stream to customer and validate in background, emitting a validation event if fails. 3) roll a canary that disables sync validation for 10% of traffic. 4) force route to fallback model that doesn't use tools if they prefer lower latency.

aj: I verified option 2 locally — patch makes schema-validator run on a separate thread and returns stream immediately. p95 drops back to baseline in my tests. caveat: we need to add compensating telemetry so any validation failures generate alerts and we can re-ingest corrected outputs.

linda: ops ask: is there a config flag we can flip without deploy? if not, what's the timeline?

maria-g: add `async_schema_validation` prod feature flag via runtime config. I can push a config change to feature/flagsengine; should be immediate (no binary deploy) for router nodes that check config every 30s. will coordinate with releases.

samir: I'll prepare a limited canary rollout: disable sync validation for routes matching customer Acme and for 5% random sample. monitor p95/p99 and error rates for 30m before widening. ETA ~30m to start canary.

cs-jen: told Acme we can do route override and will update them in ~45m. they accepted temporary validation disable for their account. keeping them updated.

aj: additional longer-term fixes: 1) move schema validation into model runtime with native bindings (reduce marshalling overhead), 2) add schema pre-compile step so validation hot path is just function calls, 3) route-level predictive sampling to pre-warm validators for heavy customers, 4) rework KV prefix cache to validate after cache hit so we don't invalidate.

maria-g: note for postmortem: instrument per-route validation latency, count of async vs sync validations, and number of retries caused by validation-timeouts. add alert: p99 validation latency > 100ms for 5m -> pager.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-tool-schema-latency. severity=high. links: https://inc.redwood/INC-2026

router-bot: canary rollout started at 1967000200 for route filter: account.acme || random<0.05. monitor endpoints: /ops/latency, /ops/validator-errors.

linda: after canary p95 for affected routes dropped ~35ms and p99 reduced more significantly. no evidence of increased validation failures in first 20m. customer confirms improvement and reduced retry rates.

cs-jen: closing loop with Acme. they asked for a postmortem + SLA credit evaluation; I'll capture impacts and send to finance/sales.

maria-g: follow-ups: - prod toggle for async validation (done) - add validation metrics to console UI per-route - schedule infra work to move validator into model runtime (EPIC-validators) - add per-customer override UI in Console.

aj: notes for reproducibility: when testing locally use a 8k token budget and a tool that returns ~1-2KB JSON; synthetic load exaggerates validation cost. command to reproduce load test: `hey -n 500 -c 50 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -D ./payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

cs-jen: thanks team — customer happy for now. filing final ticket with timeline + mitigations. :white_check_mark:
